options: Components arranged on one single loop
Each component on its own branch
questions.explanation: In series, all components line up on the one loop — beads on a single string.
questions.misconception: The branch layout is the parallel circuit, not series.

questions.prompt: In a series circuit, the current at the first bulb compared with current at the last bulb is...
questions.explanation: One loop means identical amperes at every point — the same electrons pass each bulb.
questions.misconception: That current 'spends itself' along the way is a real misconception.

questions.prompt: A 3 V battery feeds three equal series bulbs. About how many volts does each bulb see?
questions.explanation: Series splits the supply volts across the bulbs, so 3 V ÷ 3 = 1 V per bulb.
questions.misconception: Each bulb seeing the full battery voltage is the parallel misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: You unscrew one bulb from a series chain. The other bulbs...
questions.explanation: Breaking any link opens a series loop's only road, so the whole loop stops.
questions.misconception: The 'one bulb fails, others survive' behavior is the signature of parallel circuits.

questions.prompt: Adding a third bulb in series makes the existing bulbs...
questions.explanation: Every extra series bulb adds total resistance, cutting the shared current — everyone dimmer.
questions.misconception: More bulbs feel like more power; in series they starve each other.
